name: Quadrille

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated from 17th-century military horse parades and was introduced to French ballrooms around 1760.
It gained immense popularity in 1816 when Lady Jersey brought it to English high society, eventually becoming a symbol of the 19th-century European ballroom.
on_screen: Map: France · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Historically a courtly social dance, it is now performed at military galas, historical balls, and regional folk festivals such as the Brazilian Festa Junina.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Four couples form a square, facing the center.
The dance consists of five or six figures (Pantalon, Été, Poule, Trénis/Pastourelle, Finale).
Dancers perform steps such as chassé, jeté, and balancé, with figures often repeated by head and side couples.
Watch for Chaine des Dames, Dos-à-dos.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (8qXaUL6K2bk)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Four couples in a square, facing the center
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music is typically in 2/4 or 6/8 time.
Historically, it was played by orchestras using violins and woodwinds, though folk variants often utilize the accordion or diatonic organetto.
Listen for the Violin, Piano, Accordion, Organetto.
The pulse is 2/4 or 6/8.
A structured, rhythmic sound characterized by clear, repetitive 8-measure phrases, often incorporating melodies from contemporary operas or popular songs.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned
Listen later: Fledermaus-Quadrille — Johann Strauss (Sohn)
Waveform or rhythm-pattern graphic: Standard 8-measure themes

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: In the 19th century, the quadrille was a formal ballroom event requiring elegant evening wear.
In modern folk contexts, costumes vary by region, often reflecting local traditional dress.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Philippe Musard ('The Napoleon of the Quadrille'), Isaac Strauss, and the dance master Trenitz, who invented the Trénis figure.
Variants include the Lancers, the Viennese quadrille, the Jamaican 'campstyle' quadrille, the Brazilian quadrilha, and the Corsican 'U Quadrigliu Corsu'.
Derived from the French contredanse; influenced the development of American square dance, Cape Breton square dance, and Irish set dance.

scenes.title: Family tree
